newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU farm incomes rise 4.3 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: EU farm incomes rise 4.3 pct in 1996.

text.p: Farm incomes in the European Union rose by 4.3 percent in 1996, the third successive year of growth, Eurostat, the EU statistical office, said on Wednesday.
The increase follows rises of 3.7 percent in 1995 and 9.8 percent in 1994.
But, the average increase for the EU masks widely differing situations between sectors and member states.
Potato prices slumped by 38.5 percent, cereals prices fell by 7.2 percent and sugarbeet by 0.9 percent but prices for wine and olive oil rose by 3.1 percent and 13.5 percent respectively.
Cattle prices fell 14.1 percent as demand dropped as a result of the mad cow crisis but pig and sheep prices climbed by 9.6 percent and 9.4 percent respectively.
Spanish farmers enjoyed a 21.5 percent income increase, the biggest in the EU, as crop volumes rebounded after four years of drought. Farmers incomes also rose in nine other EU countries.
But Austrian and British farmers suffered income falls of 7.0 and 5.2 percent respectively. Greek, Swedish and Irish farmers experienced lower declines in income.
